title: Prefixset eviction sensitivity harness and automated regression alerts
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Build a reproducible load-testing harness that measures eviction-induced sensitivity of the prefix cache across hit-rate, p95 decode latency, tokens/sec, and memory footprint. Focus on realistic prefix distributions + aggressive eviction scenarios to discover brittle kernel scheduling or cache-coherence regressions. The harness should be able to: 1) synthesize prefixsets with configurable skew (Zipf alpha), prefix length distributions, and temporal locality; 2) run multi-concurrency traffic (1-128 concurrent streams) with variable request sizes (64-4096 tokens); 3) record fine-grained traces: per-request server-side p50/p95/p99 decode latencies, tokens/sec, KV cache hit/miss counts, cold-warm startup behavior, eviction counts, memory RSS and GPU memory per worker; 4) support deterministic seeding for regression repros; 5) integrate with our perf-regressions pipeline to auto-detect changes vs baseline and create Linear tickets when thresholds are exceeded. The initial phase will implement three primary scenarios: a) steady-state with low churn (stable working set), b) steady-state with bursty hotset shifts (80% of requests target 10% new prefixes every 5 minutes), and c) adversarial eviction pattern (round-robin prefix churn designed to maximize cold fills). We will instrument the harness to export metrics to Prometheus and push traces to Jaeger; test runs must produce an artifact bundle (metrics CSV, flamegraphs, request logs, a small reproducible workload spec).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run end-to-end in CI and produce artifact bundle for each job (metrics CSV + trace links)
Three scenarios implemented and verified against local baseline within ±3% of expected tokens/sec on our staging cluster
Regression detector integrated: when decode_p95 increases by >15% with hit_rate drop <2% or hit_rate drops by >5% with any p95 regression, pipeline files a Linear ticket with artifacts
Deterministic replay: same random seed + cluster config produces p95 within ±5% over repeated runs
Dashboard: new runtime-kv-prefixset dashboard populated with live run timeseries and histogram panels for p95 and hit rate

implementation_plan: Week 1: implement workload generator (zipf alpha, prefix lengths, locality windows) and deterministic seeding
Week 2: add instrumentation (Prometheus exporter + Jaeger traces) and artifact bundling; implement three scenarios
Week 3: integrate regression detector and CI job; create dashboard and baseline run
Week 4: run cross-instance sweep (g4dn/g5/rtx6000 equiv) and file follow-ups for any kernel-level findings
risks: Adversarial patterns may trigger unrelated scheduler or GPU driver variability — noise could obscure root cause
Large artifact bundles may increase CI storage costs; we will apply retention and sampling rules
Comparing tokens/sec across instance types requires careful normalization; risk of false positives if not normalized
